q: 1. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from
explain: For a right-handed draftsman, light from the left prevents the shadow of the hand and pencil from falling on the area being drawn.

q: 2. The isometric length of the edge of a cube is
explain: In isometric projection every edge is foreshortened to about 0.815 times its true length, so the isometric length is always less than the actual length.

q: 3. Drawing is the Engineers'
explain: A drawing conveys shape, size and construction information graphically, so it is called the universal language of engineers.

q: 4. The needle point of the compass should be…… the lead point.
explain: The needle point must be slightly longer than the pencil lead so the needle penetrates the paper while the lead still touches the surface to draw the arc.

q: 5. Axonometric projection is a special type of
explain: Axonometric projection is a single-plane orthographic projection in which the object is tilted to show three faces at once; isometric is one of its sub-types.

q: 6. The paper size of A4 is
explain: As per ISO 216 A-series standard, A4 measures 210 mm × 297 mm.

q: 7. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: The parallel ruling straight edge slides on wires/rollers fixed to the board and is used to draw a series of parallel horizontal lines.

q: 8. Vertical lines are drawn
explain: Standard drafting practice is to draw vertical lines from top to bottom for better control and visibility of the line being drawn.

q: 9. The width of the standard A-series drawing paper such as A4, A3, A2 … is
options: 1/√2 times the length of the paper
1/√3 times the length of the paper
1/√4 times the length of the paper
1/√5 times the length of the paper
explain: The A-series is designed so length:width = √2:1, i.e. the width is 1/√2 times the length, preserving the aspect ratio when the sheet is halved.

q: 10. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a sighting/surveying instrument used with a plane table, not a drawing-board hand tool.

q: 11. Working drawing is prepared not for
explain: Working drawings give graphical/dimensional information for construction, estimation and layout, but written specifications are prepared as a separate document.

q: 12. One method of preparing perspective view of an object is
explain: The vanishing point method locates the points at which parallel receding lines appear to converge, and is a standard technique for constructing perspective views.

q: 13. Free hand sketching can be done only when one has
explain: Good freehand sketching needs skill (proficiency), repeated practice, and patience together, not any single quality alone.

q: 14. The preparation of a successful drawing depends on the ……… of drawing sheet.
explain: A well-planned layout (placement of views, title block, margins) ensures the drawing is clear, uncluttered and easy to read.

q: 15. The proportion by which the actual size of an object is enlarged or reduced in drawing is simply known as
explain: This proportion, drawing size to actual size, is by definition called the scale of the drawing.

q: 16. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: The complete orthographic (glass-box) system generally uses six principal views: front, top, bottom, left, right and rear.

q: 17. Drawing board is made of
explain: Well-seasoned soft wood is used because it is light, easy to work, and allows drawing pins to be pushed in easily without warping.

q: 18. During drawing stock of T-square is placed
options: adjoining the working edge of the board
adjoining the sliding edge of the board
explain: The stock of the T-square is held firmly against the board's working (left) edge so the blade slides accurately for drawing horizontal lines.

q: 19. Set squares are not used to draw
explain: Set squares draw straight vertical, inclined and parallel lines in combination with a T-square; horizontal lines are drawn using the T-square itself, not by the set square alone.

q: 20. The diameter of semi-circle is called
explain: A protractor is a semicircular scale, and its straight diametral edge is referred to as the base of the protractor.

q: 21. Drawing pins/cello tapes are used to
explain: Pins and tape are fastening aids used to hold the drawing sheet firmly on the drawing board.

q: 22. When only one drawing is to be made then its position should be
explain: A single drawing is centred on the sheet so the layout is balanced and there is equal margin all around.

q: 23. Working space on the drawing paper is determined by
explain: The border line marks the usable working area of the sheet, separating it from the margin.

q: 24. The edge of the board on which T-square is made to slide is called
explain: The edge of the drawing board against which the T-square stock slides to guide the blade is called the working edge.

q: 25. To prevent warping of the board ……. are created at its back.
explain: Battens fixed across the back of the board resist warping caused by changes in humidity and temperature.

q: 26. The two parts of T-square are
explain: A T-square consists of a short stock (that slides along the board edge) and a long blade (used for ruling lines).

q: 27. Angles in multiples of 15° are constructed by the combined use of
explain: Combining a T-square (0°/horizontal) with 45° and 30°-60° set squares lets you construct any angle that is a multiple of 15°.

q: 28. To draw or measure angles, we use
explain: A protractor is the graduated instrument specifically designed for measuring and marking angles.

q: 29. Which of the following is attached to the compass used to draw large size circle
explain: A lengthening bar is fitted to a compass leg to extend its reach for drawing circles of large radius.

q: 30. Circles of small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: A bow compass has a fine adjusting screw that allows precise setting for drawing small circles accurately.

q: 31. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD perspective transformations rely on vector analysis to compute projections of 3D coordinates onto the picture plane.

q: 32. Measurements from scale to the drawing are transferred with the aid of
explain: A divider (with two pointed legs) is used to step off and transfer measured distances from the scale directly onto the drawing.

q: 33. The working edge of T-square is used to
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square's working (blade) edge is used both to draw horizontal parallel lines and as a guide/base on which a set square rests to draw vertical/inclined lines.

q: 34. For drawing thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened in the form of
explain: A chisel-edged pencil point maintains a consistent thin line width over long strokes, unlike a conical point which wears unevenly.

q: 35. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the
explain: A drafting machine integrates the functions of a T-square, set squares, scale and protractor into a single adjustable device.

q: 36. Circle and arcs are drawn by means of a
explain: A compass is the standard instrument for drawing circles and circular arcs of a set radius.

q: 37. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called
explain: The view obtained by projecting an object onto the horizontal plane (viewed from above) is called the plan.

q: 38. Set squares are used to draw
explain: Used alone or with a T-square, set squares can draw vertical lines, inclined lines at fixed angles, and sets of parallel lines.

q: 39. The purpose of making the drawing board with seasoned soft wood
options: for fixing of drawing paper with the help of drawing pin
explain: Soft wood lets drawing pins be pushed in and removed easily to fix the paper without damaging the board surface.

q: 40. The most important material for drawing is
explain: Paper (the drawing surface) and pencil (the marking tool) are the two most basic and essential materials for any drawing.

q: 41. Tracing paper is also named as
explain: Tracing paper, a thin transparent paper used for tracing drawings, is also commonly called drafting vellum.

q: 42. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is obtained by
explain: The isometric scale factor is 0.815, so multiplying the true length by 0.815 gives the foreshortened isometric length.

q: 43. The natural details are presented on
explain: Topographic maps show natural features such as terrain, rivers and vegetation, while cadastral maps show property boundaries.

q: 44. Free hand sketch is normally used for
explain: Freehand sketches are quick and rough, so they are mainly used to record and communicate initial concepts and ideas.

q: 45. In case of aligned method of dimensioning, they can be readable form
options: bottoms and right side of drawing sheet
bottoms and left side of drawing sheet
bottoms and top side of drawing sheet
explain: In the aligned system, dimension figures are oriented so they can be read from the bottom or the right-hand side of the sheet.

q: 46. In case of unidirectional method of dimensioning, they can be read from
options: bottom side of drawing sheet only
right side of drawing sheet only
top side of drawing sheet only
left side of drawing sheet only
explain: In the unidirectional system all dimension figures are written horizontally so they can be read only from the bottom of the sheet.

q: 47. The main objective of writing letters/alphabets on the drawing is to make the drawing
explain: Lettering adds notes, dimensions and titles, making the drawing more informative and complete.

q: 48. Working drawings are also referred to as
explain: Working drawings contain the full details needed to build the object/structure, so they are also called construction drawings.

q: 49. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed
explain: In perspective projection, the transparent picture plane is positioned between the observer's eye (station point) and the object.

q: 50. Normally perspective projection is used by
explain: Because it shows an object realistically as the eye sees it, perspective projection is favoured for marketing/presentation illustrations by manufacturers.

q: 51. The representation of any matter by some sign or marks on the drawing is known as
explain: Standard symbols used to represent materials, features or objects on a drawing are called conventions.

q: 52. Picture plane is
explain: In perspective projection the picture plane, on which the image is formed, is taken as a vertical plane.

q: 53. Ground plane is
explain: The ground plane, representing the surface on which the observer and object stand, is horizontal.

q: 54. Stock of T-square makes an angle with working edge
explain: The stock is fixed perpendicular (90°) to the blade so it registers squarely against the board's working edge.

q: 55. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: The full glass-box system of orthographic projection generally uses six principal views.

q: 56. An engineer's scale would be used to measure lines on a drawing where the scale factor reads
explain: An engineer's scale is graduated in decimal (engineering) units such as 1 inch = 100 feet, unlike an architect's scale which uses fractional feet-inch scales.

q: 57. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45° with
explain: Section (hatching) lines are conventionally drawn at 45° to the principal outline/main line of the sectioned surface.

q: 58. The techniques for free hand sketch to drawing straight line is
explain: Marking the two end points first and then joining them with a light stroke gives a straighter freehand line.

q: 59. One plane projection is
explain: Both axonometric and oblique projections are pictorial projections formed on a single plane, unlike multi-view orthographic projection.

q: 60. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called
explain: The point where the x, y (and z) axes meet is by definition called the origin.

q: 61. Isometric projection, all distances are approximately this percentage of their size
explain: The isometric reduction factor of 0.815 corresponds to roughly 80% of the true size.

q: 62. In case of diametric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: In dimetric projection two of the three axes make equal angles with the picture plane (are equally inclined), while the third differs.

q: 63. Topographic map is used to represent the
explain: Topographic maps primarily depict natural features of the terrain such as elevation, rivers and vegetation.

q: 64. Concept drawing is normally provided for the work of
explain: Concept drawings present the initial design idea and are prepared before construction begins.

q: 65. As built drawing is normally constructed
explain: As-built drawings record the actual completed work and any deviations from the design, so they are prepared after construction.

q: 66. To facilitate extension, entries in the table should begain from
explain: Filling tables from bottom upward leaves room at the top for later entries, allowing the table to be extended easily.

q: 67. The hardness of the pencil lead increase as numeral letter H
explain: In the pencil grading scale, a higher number before 'H' (e.g., 4H vs 2H) indicates a harder, lighter lead.

q: 68. A machine which is designed to perform the function of T-square, set square, scale and protractor is
explain: A drafting machine combines the functions of a T-square, set squares, scale and protractor in one adjustable head unit.

q: 69. The needle point of the compass should be .......than the lead point
explain: The needle point is set slightly longer so it stays anchored in the paper while the lead point traces the circle.

q: 70. Chisel pencils are used to draw
explain: A chisel-shaped lead maintains a uniform thin line and is best suited for ruling straight lines.

q: 71. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: The parallel ruling straight edge slides vertically on the board to draw a series of accurate horizontal lines.
